---
title: Deployment workflows
description: Deploy generated files, local directories, or linked Git projects through the same SDK interface, and handle progress, cancellation, and prompts.
---

The examples on this page accept either an `OpenshipClient` or a native `ScopedShip`. Create one using the
[remote guide](/docs/api/sdk/client) or [native guide](/docs/api/sdk/native). Both call the same source and
deployment operations.

## Deploy generated files

Use `deploy()` for files produced by your application or an AI coding workflow. It stages the source,
detects build configuration, creates or selects the project, and submits the deployment.

```ts title="deploy-generated.mts"
import type { OpenshipClient, ScopedShip } from "openship";

export async function deployGenerated(api: OpenshipClient | ScopedShip) {
  const submitted = await api.deploy({
    name: "generated-site",
    source: {
      type: "files",
      files: {
        "index.html": "<h1>Deployed from code</h1>",
        "style.css": "body { font-family: system-ui; }",
      },
    },
    onStep: (message) => console.log(message),
  });
  const outcome = await api.deployment(submitted.deployment_id).wait({ timeoutMs: 120_000 });
  return { submitted, outcome };
}
```

File keys are relative source paths. Values may be strings or `Uint8Array` data. Generated inputs are
copied before asynchronous identity checks and dispatch. Execution still requires a configured provider
and appropriate project/deployment permissions.

`deploy()` returns `deployment_id`, `project_id`, and optional `configDiagnostics`. Submission does not
mean the workload is ready. Inspect `wait()`'s outcome before reporting success to your user.

## Deploy a directory

```ts title="deploy-directory.mts"
import { resolve } from "node:path";
import type { OpenshipClient, ScopedShip } from "openship";

export async function deployDirectory(
  api: OpenshipClient | ScopedShip,
  directory: string,
  projectId?: string,
) {
  return api.deploy({
    projectId,
    source: { type: "directory", path: resolve(directory) },
  });
}
```

The remote client packages files on the calling machine and uploads them to the API. Native directory
sources must be inside an explicit `policy.sourceRoots` entry. Directory packing enforces path, entry,
and size limits, rejects escaping or cyclic symlinks and special files, and excludes `.git`,
`node_modules`, and `.DS_Store` while retaining build outputs. A system `tar` executable is not required.

| `deploy()` option | Purpose                                                                                                         |
| ----------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `source`          | Required `{ type: "files", files }` or `{ type: "directory", path }`.                                           |
| `name`            | Suggested project name; source detection can provide a name.                                                    |
| `projectId`       | Target an existing authorized project instead of creating a new one.                                            |
| `environment`     | `production` or `preview`.                                                                                      |
| `serverId`        | Target a registered, authorized server. Omit to use the configured target.                                      |
| `serviceIds`      | Select detected services to deploy.                                                                             |
| `onStep`          | Receive source-workflow progress messages. Deployment runtime logs use the event methods below.                 |
| `signal`          | Abort source-workflow work where supported. It does not roll back a deployment that has already been submitted. |

## Deploy a linked Git project

Git deployments use `deployments.create()` after the project has a configured source:

```ts title="deploy-git.mts"
import type { OpenshipClient, ScopedShip } from "openship";

export async function deployGit(api: OpenshipClient | ScopedShip, projectId: string) {
  const submitted = await api.deployments.create({
    projectId,
    branch: "main",
    environment: "production",
  });
  return api.deployment(submitted.deployment_id).wait({ timeoutMs: 120_000 });
}
```

`CreateDeploymentInput` also supports `commitSha`, `serverId`, `forceAll`, `serviceIds`, `smartRoute`, and
`refresh`. Use `deployments.prepare()` to inspect source configuration before submission. Advanced build
flows can use `sources.stage()`, `sources.scan()`, `projects.ensure()`, and `deployments.buildAccess()`;
the high-level `deploy()` composes those existing operations.

## Wait, decisions, and cancellation

`deployment(id)` returns a handle with `get()`, `status()`, `wait()`, `events()`, `cancel()`, `respond()`,
and `rollback()`. The handle does not own the deployment or an installation.

`wait()` polls persisted build status. Its outcome includes `status`, `success`, `decisionPending`,
`cancellationPending`, and optional `prompt`, `message`, or `warning`. `ready` and `no_changes` are successful;
failure, cancellation, rejection, partial failure, or an unanswered decision must be handled by your caller.

Without `onPrompt`, an outstanding prompt returns an `action_required` outcome so your application can
ask for a decision. To integrate your own decision UI:

```ts title="deployment-decisions.mts"
import type { OpenshipClient, PromptPayload, ScopedShip } from "openship";

export async function waitWithDecisions(
  api: OpenshipClient | ScopedShip,
  deploymentId: string,
  chooseAction: (prompt: PromptPayload) => Promise<string>,
  signal?: AbortSignal,
) {
  return api.deployment(deploymentId).wait({
    timeoutMs: 120_000,
    signal,
    onPrompt: chooseAction,
  });
}
```

Return an action ID offered by the prompt; the SDK validates it before submitting the response. A callback
should reflect your application's explicit decision policy. It need not automatically approve a build gate.

Aborting a wait or reaching its timeout stops observation. To request execution cancellation, call
`deployment(id).cancel()` and inspect the subsequent status. Cancellation may remain pending while the
underlying operation settles. It is not a rollback of resources created before submission.

## Read progress events

```ts title="deployment-events.mts"
import { consumeDeploymentEvents, type OpenshipClient, type ScopedShip } from "openship";

export async function readDeploymentLogs(
  api: OpenshipClient | ScopedShip,
  deploymentId: string,
  signal: AbortSignal,
) {
  return consumeDeploymentEvents(api.deployment(deploymentId).events({ signal }), (event) => {
    if (event.log) process.stdout.write(event.log);
  });
}
```

Raw events have an `event` name and serialized `data`. `consumeDeploymentEvents()` decodes payloads and
log chunks and collects stream hints. An event stream ending is not proof of deployment success; use
persisted status or `wait()` for the outcome. Pass an abort signal, or stop iteration, to release the stream.
Durable event replay across worker restarts is not implemented.

Other operation groups expose streams for service/project logs, server installation, analytics usage,
jobs, and backup/restore progress. See the [method reference](/docs/api/sdk/reference).

## Iterate paginated results

```ts title="iterate-projects.mts"
import { iteratePages, type OpenshipClient, type ScopedShip } from "openship";

export async function listProjectIds(api: OpenshipClient | ScopedShip, signal?: AbortSignal) {
  const ids: string[] = [];
  for await (const project of iteratePages((page) => api.projects.list(page), {
    perPage: 50,
    signal,
  })) {
    ids.push(project.id);
  }
  return ids;
}
```

`iteratePages()` accepts a named list method returning a page with `data` and optional pagination metadata.
It does not apply to methods that return a plain array. Access filtering remains part of the shared list
operation on every page.
